Item 1. Business

Acme Robotics designs and sells warehouse robots to logistics companies. The company operates two reportable segments: Robots and Services. Robots sells autonomous picking machines, and Services sells maintenance subscriptions and fleet software.

As of the end of fiscal 2025, Acme Robotics had approximately 4,200 full-time employees, most of them in engineering and field service.

Our customers include third-party logistics providers, grocery chains, and parcel carriers in North America and Europe. We sell through a direct sales force and a small number of resellers.

Item 1A. Risk Factors

We depend on a single supplier for the lidar sensors used in every robot. If that supplier cannot deliver, production would stop until we qualify an alternative, which could take more than nine months.

We depend on our chief executive officer and a small team of engineers. Losing key personnel could slow product development and hurt our results.

Export controls may restrict sales of our robots and software to certain countries, and new restrictions could reduce our revenue outside North America.

Competition in warehouse automation is intense. Larger competitors may offer lower prices or bundle robots with warehouse management software.

Item 1C. Cybersecurity

Our cybersecurity program is led by the Chief Information Security Officer, who reports quarterly to the Audit Committee of the Board of Directors. We assess cybersecurity risk through annual penetration tests performed by an outside firm and continuous monitoring of our fleet software.

The Audit Committee oversees cybersecurity risk and receives reports on incidents, threat assessments, and remediation progress at each regular meeting.

Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations

Total revenue grew 18% to $2.4 billion in fiscal 2025, driven by higher robot unit shipments to grocery customers and a 31% increase in Services subscriptions.

Robots$1,700$1,48015%

Gross margin fell to 41% from 44% because of higher lidar sensor costs and expedited freight in the first half of the year.

Item 7A. Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk

We are exposed to interest rate risk on our variable-rate credit facility. A 100 basis point increase in interest rates would increase annual interest expense by approximately $6 million.

We are exposed to foreign currency exchange rate risk on euro-denominated sales, which we partly hedge with forward contracts with maturities of up to twelve months.
